title: Complete f17r graft-method account: preparation, shared seasonal method scope and graft-specific refusal
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A new complete conditional reading of the already-owned ZL f17r.4–6 paragraph retains RAW375’s nine central meanings and assigns fourteen new whole-form meanings to its formerly unknown positions. Four clauses select stock/donor, prepare the stock, prescribe two shoot methods in spring or bark budding in summer, and conditionally exclude a product of a refused graft. All 23 forms are singletons here; this is extensive disclosed fitting, not vocabulary recovery. The whole uncertain tcho@154; is preserved and guessed as one unit; IT and report-projection differences stay separate.

complete_reading: Select a stock and a donor. Prepare the receiving part of the first by a cut. Methods of grafting, for that stock and donor: with a shoot from the donor, insert into a split or between inner bark and wood in spring; bud by inserting a piece of the donor’s bark in summer. If the receiving stock refuses the graft under consideration, no product of that graft follows.

complete_clause_partition.reading: Select a stock and a donor.
complete_clause_partition.effect: Introduce ordered participants [A,B] and their roles. Selection does not mean uprooting the stock or transporting either plant.

complete_clause_partition.reading: Prepare the receiving part of the first by a cut.
complete_clause_partition.effect: The receiving part belongs to stock A. Keep the donor B and donor material distinct. No exact cut dimensions, instrument or physical geometry are invented.

complete_clause_partition.reading: For that stock and donor, the two shoot-insertion methods are prescribed in spring; bark budding is prescribed in summer.
complete_clause_partition.effect: Declare alternative method instructions, not three successive executed grafts. The first two methods share A,B and the selected shoot argument; budding takes a bark piece from the same donor B, as explicitly included in the inherited cthey meaning.

complete_clause_partition.reading: If that stock refuses the graft under consideration, no product of that graft follows.
complete_clause_partition.tree: FOR_EACH_METHOD_CASE E: IF REFUSES(A,E) THEN NOT_EXISTS(PRODUCT_OF(E))
complete_clause_partition.effect: The conditional applies to the currently considered method case from C3. It does not assert refusal actually occurred, does not kill stock A and does not deny its own ordinary fruit.

finite_grammar.account: SELECT_PAIR PREPARATION METHOD_ACCOUNT REFUSAL_RULE. These four structural categories define the full account here; physical line IDs are not parser selectors.
finite_grammar.select_pair: SELECT STOCK_NOUN AND DONOR_NOUN introduces an ordered pair of two distinct role-bound plants A and B. The order is preserved for the explicit FIRST reference.
finite_grammar.preparation: PREPARE RECEIVING_PART OF_FIRST BY CUT resolves FIRST to the current ordered pair’s first member. The part selector creates a part of that bound plant, not a third unnamed stock.
finite_grammar.method_account: METHODS STOCK_ROLE DONOR_ROLE SHOOT_SOURCE SHOOT_METHOD+ SEASON BARK_METHOD SEASON. The stock/donor role nouns refer to the latest participants of those declared roles; they do not introduce replacements.
finite_grammar.scope_main: A postposed season applies to every contiguous, still-unscoped method of the current material class immediately before it. It closes that method group. Thus SPRING covers both shoot methods, and SUMMER covers BARK_BUD. The role and donor bindings persist across the group boundary.
finite_grammar.part_binding: SHOOT_SOURCE selects donor material S with origin B. Both shoot-method alternatives consume S. BARK_BUD intrinsically selects a bark piece T with origin B because the inherited whole-form meaning explicitly includes that material. S and T are different material roles in different method alternatives; a branch cannot silently reuse a whole shoot as a bark piece.
finite_grammar.modality: METHODS creates a set of licensed instruction alternatives. Reading the list does not execute all members. The account does not state an actual season, a chosen method or a completed graft. An evaluator may instantiate those explicit parameters to compute the instructions and conditional consequences.
finite_grammar.refusal_rule: IF REFUSES GRAFT NO PRODUCT reads with the active receiving stock as subject. GRAFT is the method case E under consideration from the current method account; PRODUCT means PRODUCT_OF(E). The final rule is universally applicable to each of those method cases, not an assertion of a fourth graft.
finite_grammar.instruction_scope: Only the season conditions actually expressed are evaluated. A method lacking a license in this account is not thereby botanically impossible. A false refusal condition leaves product existence unspecified; do not infer automatic success.
new_assumptions: Role-noun recurrence across different forms shol/cthy and qor/chor resolves the same A/B pair. This is a new explicit anaphoric grammar, not a discovered synonym dictionary.
The postposed spring term has shared scope over the two contiguous shoot methods; the summer term closes the budding method. No written disjunction has been independently identified.
The final five groups form a graft-specific conditional rule over the method alternatives. This is a new complete guess, not a source-labeled hidden outcome.

The receiving-part preparation is linked to the first participant through the newly guessed som=of the first. Generic cutting is a source-inspired preparation assumption, not an independently read feature or measured prerequisite.
A selected method and season are instruction parameters. No unstated actual season, favorable compatibility or executed operation is supplied as a result oracle.

content_operations_and_complete_conseque.common_insert: INSERT(receiver=A, donor_material=P, interface=I) is shared by the two spring methods. SPLIT_INSERT fixes I=split; INNER_BARK_INSERT fixes I=between inner bark and wood. Both retain origin(P)=B and the same prepared receiving plant A.
content_operations_and_complete_conseque.budding: BARK_BUD retains A and B but takes the bark-piece material specified by its own inherited meaning. It is not another application to the first detached shoot merely because the donor remains the same.
content_operations_and_complete_conseque.season_outputs_main: In the account’s two named-season domain, SPRING licenses the two shoot-insertion alternatives; SUMMER licenses the bark-budding alternative. These are written-instruction permissions, not claims that the other methods are physically impossible in those seasons.
content_operations_and_complete_conseque.refusal_output: For any selected method case E, REFUSES(A,E) makes PRODUCT_OF(E) unavailable. This affects the same proposed graft, while the stock’s own independent growth/products remain unconstrained. When refusal is false, the text alone does not prove graft success.
two_reused_input_cells: With the same A,B and donor shoot S in spring, the split and inner-bark methods share the INSERT signature but require different receiver interfaces. Neither may silently replace the donor or stock.

With the same A,B under summer, the budding method uses a bark-piece argument from B and has a different season license from the spring shoot methods. The final refusal rule scopes to whichever method case is considered.

The final REFUSES(A,E) → NOT_EXISTS(PRODUCT_OF(E)) dependency applies to more than one fully named method E. It cannot deny one method’s product using another method’s refusal without changing the bound E.
what_is_not_predicted: No actual choice, completed insertion or successful graft is asserted merely from listing methods.
No exact fruit trait, universal donor-trait preservation, numerical yield, time to union, or universal compatibility graph is supplied.
No independent empirical or botanical evidence selects a target meaning. The operations are an explicitly guessed meaning system.

fixed_full_rival.name: NEAREST_METHOD_SEASON_SCOPE
fixed_full_rival.retained: Same 23 literal ZL groups, every whole-word meaning, participant introduction, preparation, donor-part distinctions, three methods and final refusal rule.
fixed_full_rival.one_changed_rule: Each postposed season attaches only to the immediately preceding method. An earlier unmodified method remains an instruction with no season restriction stated in this account. This is a competing constituent/scope reading, not a deleted guard or a new word value.
fixed_full_rival.difference: SPLIT_INSERT has no season restriction in this rival and is therefore included among the instructions available in summer. INNER_BARK_INSERT remains spring-scoped and BARK_BUD summer-scoped. In the main grouped reading, SPLIT_INSERT is spring-scoped and has no summer license.
fixed_full_rival.shared_refusal: If the selected split graft is refused in the rival’s summer case, the same final conditional still excludes that graft’s product. Seasonal scope and product existence must not be conflated.
fixed_full_rival.source_comparison: The owned Columella summary assigns both shoot methods to spring, favoring the grouped interpretation as a source analogy. The alternative remains a coherent possible target reading and does not become a manuscript contradiction from that analogy alone.
fixed_full_rival.predecessor_relation: RAW375 already flags the missing written conjunction/disjunction and uncertain season scope, and retains an unscoped method-list rival. This is a concrete complete version of that attachment alternative, not an independent narrative discovery.

The most relevant old competing content is RAW368’s developmental leaf/flower/fruit, ripe seed extraction and sowing/store reading of .5. Its source-part identities remain unconfirmed; this descendant does not refute it by assigning different names.

The raw first whole and line eligibility flags are unresolved. IT changes an important last-clause boundary and last word; those differences are not automatically equivalent to the proposed ZL condition/result syntax.

A bark piece and a shoot are not interchangeable physical individuals. Binding every method to S just because shor occurs once would conflict with the inherited budding meaning; the explicit material-role rule must be implemented or the reading is incomplete.
A graft refusal does not imply the stock ceases to bear its own fruit. Likewise a non-refused method does not entail a successful product. Either inference would add an unwritten outcome.
No tool, root/leaf image feature, modern botanical fact or old q/dy/METHOD assignment confirms the new values. No numerical generation code or new source is substituted for a target grammar.
